key_insight: DADiff uses diffusion-model trajectory discrepancies to estimate source-target dynamics mismatch and adapt RL policies across domains.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to transfer controllers or policies when target-domain interaction data is scarce but dynamics differ from the training environment.
method: Model source and target next-state generation with a diffusion-based trajectory model
Measure generative trajectory deviation as a proxy for dynamics mismatch
Use the deviation for reward modification or target-data selection to adapt the policy
evidence_signal: The authors report extensive experiments across environments with different shifts, showing better performance than existing adaptation methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the diffusion model captures trajectories, so limited target data or poor generative fit could weaken mismatch estimation.
paper_title: DADiff: Diffusion-Driven Cross-Domain Policy Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning
